claims.claim: **In regularly transfused TDT, iron overload always happens**, because the body has no way to get rid of excess iron. In non-transfusion-dependent thalassaemia, increased gut absorption matters more. Excess iron damages the heart, liver (cirrhosis and cancer), growth and endocrine glands.
claims.locator: Thalassaemia International Federation (TIF), summary published in HemaSphere 6(8):e732, doi 10.1097/HS9.0000000000000732, '2021 Thalassaemia International Federation Guidelines for the Management of Transfusion-dependent Thalassemia', published 29 July 2022 (summary of the 2021 fourth edition), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9345633/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Transfusion context:** transfuse every 2–4 weeks, keeping pre-transfusion haemoglobin above 90–105 g/L (up to 110–120 g/L with cardiac complications) (A), and post-transfusion haemoglobin below 140–150 g/L (A).
claims.locator: Thalassaemia International Federation (TIF), summary published in HemaSphere 6(8):e732, doi 10.1097/HS9.0000000000000732, '2021 Thalassaemia International Federation Guidelines for the Management of Transfusion-dependent Thalassemia', published 29 July 2022 (summary of the 2021 fourth edition), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9345633/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Serum ferritin at least every 3 months** (every 1–3 months), aiming for 500 to 1000 μg/L. Base changes to therapy on the trend, not on one result.
claims.locator: Thalassaemia International Federation (TIF), summary published in HemaSphere 6(8):e732, doi 10.1097/HS9.0000000000000732, '2021 Thalassaemia International Federation Guidelines for the Management of Transfusion-dependent Thalassemia', published 29 July 2022 (summary of the 2021 fourth edition), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9345633/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Liver iron concentration (LIC) by validated, standardised MRI**, ideally the same method each time. Normal is up to 1.8 mg/g dry weight; LIC persistently over 15 mg/g dry weight is linked to a worse prognosis and liver fibrosis. Total body iron (mg/kg) is 10.6 × LIC.
claims.locator: Thalassaemia International Federation (TIF), summary published in HemaSphere 6(8):e732, doi 10.1097/HS9.0000000000000732, '2021 Thalassaemia International Federation Guidelines for the Management of Transfusion-dependent Thalassemia', published 29 July 2022 (summary of the 2021 fourth edition), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9345633/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **How often to repeat liver MRI:** every 1 or 2 years if stable at 3–7 mg/g; yearly above 7 mg/g; every 6–12 months if below 3 mg/g or falling fast.
claims.locator: Thalassaemia International Federation (TIF), summary published in HemaSphere 6(8):e732, doi 10.1097/HS9.0000000000000732, '2021 Thalassaemia International Federation Guidelines for the Management of Transfusion-dependent Thalassemia', published 29 July 2022 (summary of the 2021 fourth edition), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9345633/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Cardiac T2* MRI:** every 2 years if above 20 ms, yearly at 10–19 ms, and every 6 months below 10 ms. Below 10 ms, check cardiac function: heart failure risk is high and chelation must be intensified urgently.
claims.locator: Thalassaemia International Federation (TIF), summary published in HemaSphere 6(8):e732, doi 10.1097/HS9.0000000000000732, '2021 Thalassaemia International Federation Guidelines for the Management of Transfusion-dependent Thalassemia', published 29 July 2022 (summary of the 2021 fourth edition), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9345633/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Iron reaches the heart after the liver, and seldom before age 8** (B). Liver iron also clears faster than heart iron with chelation (B).
claims.locator: Thalassaemia International Federation (TIF), summary published in HemaSphere 6(8):e732, doi 10.1097/HS9.0000000000000732, '2021 Thalassaemia International Federation Guidelines for the Management of Transfusion-dependent Thalassemia', published 29 July 2022 (summary of the 2021 fourth edition), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9345633/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Screen regularly for iron damage to organs:** heart, liver and endocrine function, including diabetes, hypothyroidism, hypoparathyroidism and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.
claims.locator: Thalassaemia International Federation (TIF), summary published in HemaSphere 6(8):e732, doi 10.1097/HS9.0000000000000732, '2021 Thalassaemia International Federation Guidelines for the Management of Transfusion-dependent Thalassemia', published 29 July 2022 (summary of the 2021 fourth edition), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9345633/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Keep records for each patient:** the age at which regular transfusion and chelation began, and each year's blood use (mL/kg packed cells) and daily iron load (mg/kg/day).
claims.locator: Thalassaemia International Federation (TIF), summary published in HemaSphere 6(8):e732, doi 10.1097/HS9.0000000000000732, '2021 Thalassaemia International Federation Guidelines for the Management of Transfusion-dependent Thalassemia', published 29 July 2022 (summary of the 2021 fourth edition), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9345633/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Chelation has five aims:** prevention (keep body iron safe by matching excretion to transfusion intake); rescue (remove stored excess); emergency (urgent intensification for iron-induced heart failure); dose adjustment (avoid both under- and over-chelation); and adherence. Intermittent high-dose chelation does not protect continuously against labile iron and adds toxicity.
claims.locator: Thalassaemia International Federation (TIF), summary published in HemaSphere 6(8):e732, doi 10.1097/HS9.0000000000000732, '2021 Thalassaemia International Federation Guidelines for the Management of Transfusion-dependent Thalassemia', published 29 July 2022 (summary of the 2021 fourth edition), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9345633/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Three chelators are licensed:** deferoxamine (desferrioxamine), deferiprone and deferasirox. All three lower total body iron and liver iron (A).
claims.locator: Thalassaemia International Federation (TIF), summary published in HemaSphere 6(8):e732, doi 10.1097/HS9.0000000000000732, '2021 Thalassaemia International Federation Guidelines for the Management of Transfusion-dependent Thalassemia', published 29 July 2022 (summary of the 2021 fourth edition), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9345633/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Chelation improves survival and lowers heart failure risk and iron-related illness** (A). At the right dose and frequency it can balance the iron gained from transfusion (A).
claims.locator: Thalassaemia International Federation (TIF), summary published in HemaSphere 6(8):e732, doi 10.1097/HS9.0000000000000732, '2021 Thalassaemia International Federation Guidelines for the Management of Transfusion-dependent Thalassemia', published 29 July 2022 (summary of the 2021 fourth edition), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9345633/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Prevent build-up rather than rescue later** (B): iron damage is often permanent, and stored iron comes out slowly, especially once it has spread beyond the liver.
claims.locator: Thalassaemia International Federation (TIF), summary published in HemaSphere 6(8):e732, doi 10.1097/HS9.0000000000000732, '2021 Thalassaemia International Federation Guidelines for the Management of Transfusion-dependent Thalassemia', published 29 July 2022 (summary of the 2021 fourth edition), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9345633/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Response depends on dose and duration of exposure** (A) and on how fast the patient is being transfused (B).
claims.locator: Thalassaemia International Federation (TIF), summary published in HemaSphere 6(8):e732, doi 10.1097/HS9.0000000000000732, '2021 Thalassaemia International Federation Guidelines for the Management of Transfusion-dependent Thalassemia', published 29 July 2022 (summary of the 2021 fourth edition), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9345633/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Lower the dose as ferritin or liver iron falls**, because over-chelation increases side effects (B; shown most clearly with deferoxamine).
claims.locator: Thalassaemia International Federation (TIF), summary published in HemaSphere 6(8):e732, doi 10.1097/HS9.0000000000000732, '2021 Thalassaemia International Federation Guidelines for the Management of Transfusion-dependent Thalassemia', published 29 July 2022 (summary of the 2021 fourth edition), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9345633/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Tailor the regimen to the person and their current state, and work on adherence:** chelation fails if it is not taken regularly (B). Patients report better outcomes with oral than with parenteral chelation (B), and psychological wellbeing affects adherence and survival (C).
claims.locator: Thalassaemia International Federation (TIF), summary published in HemaSphere 6(8):e732, doi 10.1097/HS9.0000000000000732, '2021 Thalassaemia International Federation Guidelines for the Management of Transfusion-dependent Thalassemia', published 29 July 2022 (summary of the 2021 fourth edition), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9345633/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Cardiac iron overload needs intensified chelation, preferably two drugs together**, with or without heart dysfunction or failure (B). Chelation guided by cardiac T2* is the best way to prevent iron cardiomyopathy (B).
claims.locator: Thalassaemia International Federation (TIF), summary published in HemaSphere 6(8):e732, doi 10.1097/HS9.0000000000000732, '2021 Thalassaemia International Federation Guidelines for the Management of Transfusion-dependent Thalassemia', published 29 July 2022 (summary of the 2021 fourth edition), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9345633/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Heart function can recover within weeks** if chelation covers all 24 hours (A), but stored heart iron takes months or years to clear (A).
claims.locator: Thalassaemia International Federation (TIF), summary published in HemaSphere 6(8):e732, doi 10.1097/HS9.0000000000000732, '2021 Thalassaemia International Federation Guidelines for the Management of Transfusion-dependent Thalassemia', published 29 July 2022 (summary of the 2021 fourth edition), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9345633/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Without cardiac MRI:** a fall in left ventricular function on serial echocardiograms is a warning sign of iron toxicity and should prompt strong, sustained escalation of chelation (B).
claims.locator: Thalassaemia International Federation (TIF), summary published in HemaSphere 6(8):e732, doi 10.1097/HS9.0000000000000732, '2021 Thalassaemia International Federation Guidelines for the Management of Transfusion-dependent Thalassemia', published 29 July 2022 (summary of the 2021 fourth edition), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9345633/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Fever:** stop deferoxamine temporarily and start antibiotics promptly. Patients with iron overload can keep taking oral deferiprone or deferasirox while febrile.
claims.locator: Thalassaemia International Federation (TIF), summary published in HemaSphere 6(8):e732, doi 10.1097/HS9.0000000000000732, '2021 Thalassaemia International Federation Guidelines for the Management of Transfusion-dependent Thalassemia', published 29 July 2022 (summary of the 2021 fourth edition), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9345633/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Pregnancy:** if heart function worsens, deferoxamine can be used with caution after the first trimester.
claims.locator: Thalassaemia International Federation (TIF), summary published in HemaSphere 6(8):e732, doi 10.1097/HS9.0000000000000732, '2021 Thalassaemia International Federation Guidelines for the Management of Transfusion-dependent Thalassemia', published 29 July 2022 (summary of the 2021 fourth edition), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9345633/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Endocrine complications can reverse** when total body iron is normalised with intensive combined deferoxamine plus deferiprone (B).
claims.locator: Thalassaemia International Federation (TIF), summary published in HemaSphere 6(8):e732, doi 10.1097/HS9.0000000000000732, '2021 Thalassaemia International Federation Guidelines for the Management of Transfusion-dependent Thalassemia', published 29 July 2022 (summary of the 2021 fourth edition), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9345633/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Vitamin C (2–3 mg/kg/day)** is recommended with deferoxamine infusions, or when deficiency is proven.
claims.locator: Thalassaemia International Federation (TIF), summary published in HemaSphere 6(8):e732, doi 10.1097/HS9.0000000000000732, '2021 Thalassaemia International Federation Guidelines for the Management of Transfusion-dependent Thalassemia', published 29 July 2022 (summary of the 2021 fourth edition), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9345633/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Offer stem cell transplant early**, before iron complications develop, when an HLA-identical sibling donor is available.
claims.locator: Thalassaemia International Federation (TIF), summary published in HemaSphere 6(8):e732, doi 10.1097/HS9.0000000000000732, '2021 Thalassaemia International Federation Guidelines for the Management of Transfusion-dependent Thalassemia', published 29 July 2022 (summary of the 2021 fourth edition), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9345633/, retrieved 2026-09-23
